chunks: The Month of Ramadan is thirty days, not being deficient, ever!
And from him, from al-Hasan ibn al-Husayn, from Ibn Sinan, from Hudhayfa — similar to it.

key_terms.أَبَداً: Ever, never, absolutely — emphatic negation reinforcing the ruling
key_terms.ثَلَاثُونَ يَوْماً: Thirty days — the fixed duration asserted here as absolute
key_terms.شَهْرُ رَمَضَانَ: The month of Ramadan — the ninth month of the Islamic calendar, the month of obligatory fasting
key_terms.لَا يَنْقُصُ: Not deficient, does not decrease — a legal assertion about Ramadan's duration

ai.seo_question: How many days is the month of Ramadan according to Imam al-Sadiq?
ai.summary: Imam al-Sadiq (peace be upon him) declared that the month of Ramadan consists of thirty days without exception and never decreases. This ruling was transmitted through two separate chains of narrators, with the second chain offering a parallel transmission confirming the same ruling. In Shia jurisprudence, this hadith is cited in discussions about whether Ramadan can ever be twenty-nine days based on moon sighting or calculation.
